clue.text: It takes a canny farmer to make this creature fast!

definitions.text: It takes a canny farmer to make this creature fast!

parts.words: It takes a canny farmer to make this creature fast!
parts.note: a shrewd farmer is out to make 'a fast ...', quick easy money, and the male deer is also a creature that runs fast

explanation.surface: A tribute to the skill a farmer needs to tether or tame a lively animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests tying an animal down; the real point is the idiom 'make a fast buck', meaning to earn money quickly, which a canny farmer would like to do.
explanation.definitionFit: A male deer, rabbit or hare is called by this name, and the idiom for quick profit uses the same word for a dollar.

clue.text: Unfathomable, not like A Midsummer Night's Dream

definitions.text: not like A Midsummer Night's Dream
definitions.meaning: lacking Bottom, the weaver in Shakespeare's comedy

explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's play has a character called Bottom, so something without him is unlike the play.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit with no floor is immeasurably deep, and a play without Shakespeare's weaver Bottom lacks him.

clue.text: Manage to conceal spades in thicket

indicators.note: says the spades letter is hidden inside the word for manage

parts.note: to cope is to manage
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: Coping with hiding gardening spades among the undergrowth.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dense wood of trees or shrubs is a near-synonym of a thicket.

clue.text: Badly chip a table, like characters in a demo

indicators.note: badly says the letters of the words that follow are put together wrongly, in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Damaging a table with a chip, as though it were part of some demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demo' looks like a protest or trial run, but its letters D, E, M, O stand in the order of the alphabet, which is what the definition is pointing at.
explanation.definitionFit: The four letters of demo run in their dictionary order, so they are arranged in the sequence of the ABC.

clue.text: Lustful person flogging heroin around island?

indicators.note: places the heroin letter next to the island, at its end

parts.note: a licker is one who licks, or beats, someone
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A depraved type selling heroin around an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flogging' looks like selling drugs, but it means beating, hence LICKER.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare Elizabethan word means lecherous or greedy, so it is a synonym of lustful.

clue.text: Ben Nevis ultimately overlooks entrance to this wood

indicators.note: in a down clue the S sits above the next letter

parts.note: Ben-Hur is the epic film and novel, so Ben is followed by Hur

indicators.note: takes the final letter of the word next to it
takes the first letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: Britain's highest mountain looks down on the entrance to a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ben Nevis' looks like the Scottish mountain, but Ben is the first half of Ben-Hur and gives HUR.
explanation.definitionFit: This old word means a wooded hill or grove, found in many English place names.

clue.text: Instrument graduates need shortly to construct

parts.note: BAs are holders of Bachelor of Arts degrees
soon means shortly, in a little while

explanation.surface: Graduates will soon be needed to build a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'need' and 'to construct' are link words: the graduates and 'shortly' build the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A large woodwind with a double reed playing in the bass register is an example of a musical instrument.

clue.text: Wordy story about king upset Sackville-West

indicators.note: says the story wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: a tale is a story
K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: the letters of the writer's first name are thrown into a new order

parts.note: Vita Sackville-West was the English writer and gardener

explanation.surface: A story about a king that annoyed the writer Vita Sackville-West.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer is named by surname only; her first name, Vita, is the fodder, and 'upset' scrambles it into ATIV, while 'about' wraps the story round.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone using many words, or given to chatting, is verbose, a near-synonym of wordy.

clue.text: Attractive fashion associated with English

parts.note: a cut is the style or fashion of a garment

explanation.surface: An appealing style that people link to England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pretty or endearing is charming, a synonym of attractive.

clue.text: Liberal leader with a posh four wheeled carriage

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: and means with, joining things
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: The head of the Liberals arrives with a smart vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U are British labels for upper-class and lower-class speech and manners.
explanation.definitionFit: This horse-drawn four-wheeled vehicle has a folding hood, named after a German town.

clue.text: Reindeer by water source, one hoofing it noisily

parts.note: a tap is where water comes from at a sink
Dancer is one of Santa's reindeer in the Christmas poem

explanation.surface: One of Santa's reindeer standing by a watering place, clattering its hooves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' sets the two pieces side by side; the reindeer piece comes after the tap in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoofing is slang for dancing, and this performer's metal-plated shoes make a loud clicking on the floor.

clue.text: Divide port

definitions.meaning: to separate into parts, as a verb
a harbour city on the Croatian coast in Dalmatia

explanation.definitionFit: To cleave something is to break it apart, and the Croatian coastal city on the Adriatic bears the same name.

clue.text: Old composer fails to finish service, son having left late

indicators.note: the composer's name stops short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Verdi was the Italian opera composer

indicators.note: says that the son has departed from the word for service

parts.note: use means service, as in 'of some use'

explanation.surface: An old composer cannot complete a church service once his son walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails to finish' cuts VERDI to VERD; 'having left' takes S out of USE to leave UE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something behind schedule or past its due time is tardy, which is a synonym of the definition.

clue.text: Girl returns in coach, one leaving Paris for example

indicators.note: says the reversed girl's name sits inside the shortened coach
the numeral one, as I, departs from the word for coach

parts.note: a train is a coach in the sense of a railway carriage set
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the girl's name is read back to front

parts.note: Jo is a short girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl comes back on the coach while one passenger gets off, heading for Paris perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes Paris the French capital; here he is the prince of Troy. 'returns' gives OJ and 'one leaving' leaves TRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris, the prince who abducted Helen, was a son of King Priam and so a native of Troy.

clue.text: So the opera develops-it sets the pulse racing!

indicators.note: the words grow into something new, their letters rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The opera unfolds, and it gets the heart racing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' looks like a heartbeat, but pulses are peas and beans, which this toy fires.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's toy tube for blowing dried peas, which are pulses, at speed, sends them flying.

clue.text: Party agonising about small number needing large workforce

parts.note: Labour is the British political party

indicators.note: says the word for agonising wraps round the small number

parts.note: intense, as of pain that is acute
IV is four in Roman numerals, a small number

explanation.surface: A political party in torment over a small figure while needing a large staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A task that needs many workers relative to its machinery is described as heavy on manpower.

clue.text: Pub employee taking out a titled person?

parts.note: Bart is the abbreviation for baronet, a hereditary title
an ender is one who finishes off, or takes out, someone

explanation.surface: A pub worker escorting someone with a title on a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking out' reads as a date, but here it means killing: one who ends a baronet.
explanation.definitionFit: The person serving drinks behind the counter of a pub is its barman or barmaid.

clue.text: Description of stress in this sounds deliberate

indicators.note: the answer follows the word in, which joined to it gives the sound
says the word for deliberate is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: intentional means deliberate, done on purpose
the word in is the piece placed before the answer

explanation.surface: An account of strain in a piece that seems intentional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in this' means IN plus the answer, which when spoken resembles a word for deliberate, if only in slurred speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective describing tension or strain in a material is a word for describing stress.

clue.text: Son neglects others, going out for stroll

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are taken out of their order and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A son who ignores everybody else as he leaves the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going out' looks like part of the story of the son leaving, but it signals the rearrangement of NEGLECTSOTHERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a short walk for exercise after sitting still is the idiom's sense, much like a leisurely walk.

clue.text: Asian colossus that's captured live?

indicators.note: says the giant holds the word for live inside it

parts.note: a titan is a giant or colossus
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: A giant statue in Asia that seems to have trapped someone alive.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Tibet, the high Himalayan region, is a person from Asia.

clue.text: Travelling, hops in Tube

indicators.note: the letters travel about and land in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Journeying by hopping onto the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' looks like the London Underground, but it is a pipe for drawing liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent pipe for drawing liquid from one container into another is a kind of tube.

clue.text: Like seed-bearing plants a woman's dog brought back

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman

indicators.note: the dog's name is read in reverse

parts.note: a lab is a Labrador retriever

explanation.surface: A woman's dog is fetched home after wandering among the plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns LAB into BAL. The word 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbs are in botany seed-bearing plants without woody stems, so the adjective describes things relating to them.

clue.text: Money Poirot endlessly raised

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters are read upwards
the detective's first name loses its first and last letters

parts.note: Hercule Poirot is Agatha Christie's Belgian detective

explanation.surface: The detective's cash is constantly going up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts HERCULE to ERCUL; 'raised' reads it upwards as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This word means money, usually gain thought of as greedy or dishonourable.

clue.text: I'm young enough for anything? That's laying it on thick!

definitions.meaning: read as ..., someone past nought, not too old for nothing at all
the painting technique of applying pigment heavily so that brushstrokes stand out

explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads as I'M PAST O, with O as zero: a person who is past nothing is young enough for anything.
explanation.definitionFit: This painting technique applies pigment in a thick layer, so the exclamation describes it literally.

clue.text: Somewhat stylish, a Korean soldier's headdress

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rather fashionable Korean soldier with smart military headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall cylindrical military cap with a peak and plume is a type of soldier's hat.

clue.text: Stare stupidly when wife falls into hole

indicators.note: says the wife's letter drops inside the hole

parts.note: a gap is a hole or opening

explanation.surface: Gaping in amazement as a wife tumbles into a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: This British slang word means to gape open-mouthed, staring like a fool.

clue.text: University entrance without examination

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside, so the entrance surrounds the university letter

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal entrance to a mine

explanation.surface: Getting into university without having to sit any test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside, putting U inside ADIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An official inspection of accounts is a formal check or review, a kind of scrutiny.

clue.text: In agreement? Not I, for one

definitions.meaning: any letter that is not a vowel such as I, like B or T

explanation.definitionFit: The word means harmonious or in accord, and also any letter other than a vowel, which I is.

clue.text: In the country, wooded hollow encircled by river writer found

indicators.note: says the river's letters wrap round the country and hollow

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
Iran is the country in the Middle East
a dell is a small wooded valley

explanation.surface: A writer discovered in a wooded valley by a river, somewhere abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The Italian river fits the Italian playwright. 'In the' and 'found' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Luigi Pirandello was an Italian dramatist and novelist, author of Six Characters in Search of an Author.

clue.text: Animal stole last of fodder

parts.note: a boa is a long scarf or stole of feathers or fur

indicators.note: takes the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Some animal pinched the remaining scraps of its feed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stole' reads as a verb, but it is the noun, a scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild pig or uncastrated male pig is a mammal, so a specific example of the general term.
